+"""Automatic updates of Home Assistant Core patch releases."""
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import datetime, time, timedelta
+from enum import StrEnum
+from typing import Any, Self, TypedDict
+
+from aiohasupervisor.models import UpdateChannel
+from awesomeversion import AwesomeVersion
+import probatio
+
+from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntry
+from homeassistant.const import WEEKDAYS
+from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant, callback
+from homeassistant.helpers import config_validation as cv
+from homeassistant.helpers.storage import Store
+from homeassistant.util import dt as dt_util
+
+from .const import (
+    CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_DELAYS,
+    DEFAULT_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_DELAY,
+    DEFAULT_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_END,
+    DEFAULT_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_START,
+    OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE,
+    OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_DELAY,
+    OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WEEKDAYS,
+    OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_END,
+    OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_START,
+)
+from .coordinator import HassioMainDataUpdateCoordinator
+
+STORAGE_KEY = "hassio.auto_update"
+STORAGE_VERSION = 1
+
+# Options are stored as text, so store times the way the settings read them
+_time_string = probatio.All(cv.time, time.isoformat)
+
+
+def _validate_window(options: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Reject an empty time window; one that crosses midnight is fine."""
+    start = options.get(
+        OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_START, DEFAULT_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_START
+    )
+    end = options.get(
+        OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_END, DEFAULT_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_END
+    )
+    if start == end:
+        raise probatio.Invalid("The time window must not start and end at once")
+    return options
+
+
+AUTO_UPDATE_OPTIONS_SCHEMA = probatio.All(
+    probatio.Schema(
+        {
+            probatio.Optional(OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE): bool,
+            probatio.Optional(OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_DELAY): probatio.In(
+                CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_DELAYS
+            ),
+            probatio.Optional(OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_START): _time_string,
+            probatio.Optional(OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_END): _time_string,
+            probatio.Optional(OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WEEKDAYS): probatio.All(
+                cv.weekdays, probatio.Length(min=1)
+            ),
+        },
+        extra=probatio.ALLOW_EXTRA,
+    ),
+    _validate_window,
+)
+
+
+class AutoUpdateUnavailableReason(StrEnum):
+    """Why automatic updates are not available on this installation."""
+
+    NOT_HOME_ASSISTANT_OS = "not_home_assistant_os"
+    NOT_STABLE_CHANNEL = "not_stable_channel"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
+class AutoUpdateSettings:
+    """The user's settings for automatic Home Assistant updates."""
+
+    # None means the user has not made a choice yet
+    enabled: bool | None
+    delay: timedelta
+    window_start: time
+    window_end: time
+    weekdays: frozenset[str]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_options(cls, options: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Self:
+        """Build the settings from the hassio config entry options."""
+        return cls(
+            enabled=options.get(OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE),
+            delay=timedelta(
+                days=options.get(
+                    OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_DELAY, DEFAULT_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_DELAY
+                )
+            ),
+            window_start=time.fromisoformat(
+                options.get(
+                    OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_START,
+                    DEFAULT_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_START,
+                )
+            ),
+            window_end=time.fromisoformat(
+                options.get(
+                    OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_END,
+                    DEFAULT_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WINDOW_END,
+                )
+            ),
+            weekdays=frozenset(options.get(OPTION_CORE_AUTO_UPDATE_WEEKDAYS, WEEKDAYS)),
+        )
+
+
+class AutoUpdateStoreData(TypedDict):
+    """Stored data for automatic Home Assistant updates."""
+
+    first_seen: dict[str, str]
+
+
+def _major(version: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Return the major release of a version, like (2026, 10) for 2026.10.2."""
+    parsed = AwesomeVersion(version)
+    return (int(parsed.section(0)), int(parsed.section(1)))
+
+
+class AutoUpdateManager:
+    """Keep the state for automatic Home Assistant updates."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        hass: HomeAssistant,
+        entry: ConfigEntry,
+        coordinator: HassioMainDataUpdateCoordinator,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Initialize the manager."""
+        self._hass = hass
+        self._entry = entry
+        self._coordinator = coordinator
+        self._store: Store[AutoUpdateStoreData] = Store(
+            hass, STORAGE_VERSION, STORAGE_KEY
+        )
+        self._first_seen: dict[str, datetime] = {}
+
+    async def async_setup(self) -> None:
+        """Load the stored data and start tracking offered versions."""
+        if (data := await self._store.async_load()) is not None:
+            self._first_seen = {
+                version: datetime.fromisoformat(first_seen)
+                for version, first_seen in data["first_seen"].items()
+            }
+
+        self._async_record_offered_version()
+        self._entry.async_on_unload(
+            self._coordinator.async_add_listener(self._async_record_offered_version)
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def settings(self) -> AutoUpdateSettings:
+        """Return the current settings."""
+        return AutoUpdateSettings.from_options(self._entry.options)
+
+    @property
+    def unavailable_reason(self) -> AutoUpdateUnavailableReason | None:
+        """Return why automatic updates are unavailable, or None if available."""
+        data = self._coordinator.data
+        if data.os is None:
+            return AutoUpdateUnavailableReason.NOT_HOME_ASSISTANT_OS
+        if data.supervisor.channel != UpdateChannel.STABLE:
+            return AutoUpdateUnavailableReason.NOT_STABLE_CHANNEL
+        return None
+
+    @callback
+    def async_get_first_seen(self, version: str) -> datetime | None:
+        """Return when Supervisor first offered a version."""
+        return self._first_seen.get(version)
+
+    @callback
+    def _async_record_offered_version(self) -> None:
+        """Record when a version is first offered, and forget old majors.
+
+        The version file has no release dates, so the wait after a release
+        counts from the moment this installation first saw it. That moment
+        must never move, or the wait would start over.
+        """
+        if self.unavailable_reason is not None:
+            return
+
+        core = self._coordinator.data.core
+        if core.version is None or core.version_latest is None:
+            return
+
+        changed = False
+        if core.version_latest not in self._first_seen:
+            self._first_seen[core.version_latest] = dt_util.utcnow()
+            changed = True
+
+        running_major = _major(core.version)
+        for version in list(self._first_seen):
+            if _major(version) < running_major:
+                del self._first_seen[version]
+                changed = True
+
+        # Save right away as an entry task; unload waits for it, so a reload
+        # cannot read the store before the first-seen time is written.
+        if changed:
+            self._entry.async_create_task(
+                self._hass, self._store.async_save(self._data_to_save())
+            )
+
+    @callback
+    def _data_to_save(self) -> AutoUpdateStoreData:
+        """Return the data to store."""
+        return {
+            "first_seen": {
+                version: first_seen.isoformat()
+                for version, first_seen in self._first_seen.items()
+            }
+        }

+"""Test automatic Home Assistant updates."""

+    await hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)

+async def test_first_seen_is_set_once(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    hass_storage: dict[str, Any],
+    freezer: FrozenDateTimeFactory,
+    homeassistant_info: AsyncMock,
+) -> None:
+    """Test the first time a version is offered is recorded and never changes."""
+    first_seen = dt_util.utcnow()
+    await _setup_hassio(hass)
+    manager = hass.data[DATA_AUTO_UPDATE]
+
+    assert manager.async_get_first_seen("2026.10.2") == first_seen

+    await _refresh_main_coordinator(hass, freezer)

+
+    assert manager.async_get_first_seen("2026.10.2") == first_seen
+    assert manager.async_get_first_seen("2026.10.3") == newer_first_seen
+
+    assert hass_storage[STORAGE_KEY]["data"] == {
+        "first_seen": {
+            "2026.10.2": first_seen.isoformat(),
+            "2026.10.3": newer_first_seen.isoformat(),
+        }
+    }
+

+        await hass.async_block_till_done()

+
+

query:
Install eligible patch releases on schedule

Part of home-assistant/epics#128.

**Depends on:** home-assistant/core#186853

**Why.** This is the feature itself: pick the right patch and install it inside the user's window.

**What to do**

- Run the check at startup and every hour. Work only from current state, never from what triggered the check, so it gives the same answer whenever it runs.
- Skip the check when: disabled or paused (home-assistant/core#186857), not Home Assistant OS, not the stable channel, an update or backup is already running, or Home Assistant is in safe mode.
- Pick the target: the **newest** version that
  - is a patch of the running major (2026.10.x when on 2026.10.1)
  - has passed the wait since it was first seen
  - is not skipped (home-assistant/core#186858)
  - is not newer than the version Supervisor currently offers. If we pull a release by rolling back the version file, pending installs stop here.
- Install at most one version per run.
- If now is inside the window on an allowed weekday, ask Supervisor to install that exact version, with a backup when that setting is on.
- Spread load: each installation picks a fixed random minute inside its window and installs from that minute on.

**Where to look**

- Install: `update_core(hass, version, backup)` in `hassio/update_helper.py` already takes a version. Core makes the backup itself (`backup_core_before_update` in `hassio/backup.py`) and passes `backup=False` to Supervisor; Supervisor does the health check and rollback. `backup_core_before_update()` already uses the automatic backup settings when configured and a local manual backup otherwise, the same as the update dialog (`src/dialogs/more-info/components/update/ha-more-info-update-backup.ts` in frontend). Call it as is.
- Schedule: `async_track_time_interval` from `homeassistant/helpers/event.py`, started in `async_setup_entry` in `hassio/__init__.py`, plus one run after start.
- Running jobs: `SupervisorJobsCoordinator` in `hassio/coordinator.py` (the Core update job is `home_assistant_core_update`).
- Version compare: `AwesomeVersion`, already used in `hassio/update.py`.
- The fixed random minute per install: keep it in the store from home-assistant/core#186853 so it survives restarts.

**Done when**

- [ ] A major release is never installed automatically
- [ ] When 2026.10.2 has passed the wait but 2026.10.3 has not, 2026.10.2 is installed
- [ ] A pulled release (version file rolled back) is not installed
- [ ] A skipped version is not installed
- [ ] Nothing installs outside the window or on a disallowed weekday
- [ ] Tests cover each rule

**Not in this task:** what happens after the restart (home-assistant/core#186855), the pause switch (home-assistant/core#186857).

+    """Set up Sky Hub from a config entry."""

+        if not coordinator.data.keys() - seen_macs:
+            return
+        seen_macs.update(coordinator.data)
+        entry.async_create_background_task(
+            hass,
+            _async_check_legacy_known_devices(hass, entry, set(seen_macs)),
+            name=f"{DOMAIN} legacy known_devices check",
+        )
+
+    await _async_check_legacy_known_devices(hass, entry, seen_macs)

+    )

+    """Return the legacy conflict issue ID for this router."""

+    hass: HomeAssistant, entry: SkyHubConfigEntry, tracked: Collection[str]

+    legacy_devices = await async_load_config(

+"""Config flow for the Sky Hub integration."""
+
+from typing import Any, override
+
+from aiohttp import ClientError
+import probatio
+from pyskyqhub.skyq_hub import SkyQHub
+
+from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigFlow, ConfigFlowResult
+from homeassistant.const import CONF_HOST
+from homeassistant.helpers.aiohttp_client import async_get_clientsession
+
+from .const import DEFAULT_HOST, DOMAIN
+
+STEP_USER_DATA_SCHEMA = probatio.Schema(
+    {probatio.Required(CONF_HOST, default=DEFAULT_HOST): str}
+)
+
+
+class SkyHubConfigFlow(ConfigFlow, domain=DOMAIN):
+    """Handle a config flow for Sky Hub."""
+
+    VERSION = 1
+
+    async def _async_can_connect(self, host: str) -> bool:
+        """Check whether the router is accessible."""
+        router = SkyQHub(async_get_clientsession(self.hass), host)
+        try:
+            await router.async_connect()
+        except ClientError:
+            return False
+        return router.success_init
+
+    @override
+    async def async_step_user(
+        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
+    ) -> ConfigFlowResult:
+        """Handle the initial step."""
+        errors: dict[str, str] = {}
+
+        if user_input is not None:
+            self._async_abort_entries_match({CONF_HOST: user_input[CONF_HOST]})
+
+            if await self._async_can_connect(user_input[CONF_HOST]):
+                return self.async_create_entry(
+                    title=user_input[CONF_HOST],
+                    data=user_input,
+                )
+            errors["base"] = "cannot_connect"
+
+        return self.async_show_form(
+            step_id="user",
+            data_schema=STEP_USER_DATA_SCHEMA,
+            errors=errors,
+        )
+
+    async def async_step_import(self, import_data: dict[str, Any]) -> ConfigFlowResult:
+        """Handle import from legacy YAML configuration."""
+        self._async_abort_entries_match({CONF_HOST: import_data[CONF_HOST]})
+
+        if not await self._async_can_connect(import_data[CONF_HOST]):
+            return self.async_abort(reason="cannot_connect")
+
+        return self.async_create_entry(title=import_data[CONF_HOST], data=import_data)

+"""Fixtures for Sky Hub tests."""
+
+from collections.abc import Generator
+from typing import NamedTuple
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, patch
+
+import pytest
+from pytest_homeassistant.common import MockConfigEntry
+
+from homeassistant.components.sky_hub.const import DEFAULT_HOST, DOMAIN
+from homeassistant.const import CONF_HOST
+
+
+class MockDevice(NamedTuple):
+    """A device reported by Sky Hub."""
+
+    mac: str
+    name: str
+
+
+LAPTOP = MockDevice("AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF", "Laptop")
+PHONE = MockDevice("11:22:33:44:55:66", "Phone")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def mock_setup_entry() -> Generator[AsyncMock]:
+    """Mock config-entry setup for flow tests."""
+    with patch(
+        "homeassistant.components.sky_hub.async_setup_entry", return_value=True
+    ) as mock:
+        yield mock
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def mock_config_entry() -> MockConfigEntry:
+    """Return a Sky Hub config entry."""
+    return MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST})
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def mock_router() -> Generator[MagicMock]:
+    """Mock the Sky Hub client."""
+    with (
+        patch("homeassistant.components.sky_hub.SkyQHub", autospec=True) as client,
+        patch("homeassistant.components.sky_hub.coordinator.SkyQHub", new=client),
+        patch("homeassistant.components.sky_hub.config_flow.SkyQHub", new=client),
+    ):
+        router = client.return_value
+        router.success_init = True
+        router.async_get_skyhub_data.return_value = [LAPTOP]
+        yield router

+"""Tests for Sky Hub config flows."""
+
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+from aiohttp import ClientError, ClientPayloadError
+import pytest
+from pytest_homeassistant.common import MockConfigEntry
+
+from homeassistant.components.sky_hub.const import DEFAULT_HOST, DOMAIN
+from homeassistant.config_entries import SOURCE_IMPORT, SOURCE_USER
+from homeassistant.const import CONF_HOST
+from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
+from homeassistant.data_entry_flow import FlowResultType
+
+CONNECT_ERRORS = [
+    pytest.param(False, None, id="unsuccessful_init"),
+    pytest.param(True, ClientPayloadError("Incomplete response"), id="payload_error"),
+]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_setup_entry", "mock_router")
+async def test_successful_user_config_flow(hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
+    """Test a successful user config flow."""
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_USER}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.FORM
+    assert result["step_id"] == "user"
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
+        result["flow_id"], {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY
+    assert result["title"] == DEFAULT_HOST
+    assert result["data"] == {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_setup_entry")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("connected", "connect_error"), CONNECT_ERRORS)
+async def test_user_cannot_connect_and_retry(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    connected: bool,
+    connect_error: ClientError | None,
+) -> None:
+    """Test connection failures show errors and the user can retry successfully."""
+    mock_router.success_init = connected
+    mock_router.async_connect.side_effect = connect_error
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_USER}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.FORM
+    assert result["step_id"] == "user"
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
+        result["flow_id"], {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.FORM
+    assert result["step_id"] == "user"
+    assert result["errors"] == {"base": "cannot_connect"}
+
+    mock_router.success_init = True
+    mock_router.async_connect.reset_mock()
+    mock_router.async_connect.side_effect = None
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
+        result["flow_id"], {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY
+    assert result["title"] == DEFAULT_HOST
+    assert result["data"] == {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_setup_entry", "mock_router")
+async def test_import_creates_entry(hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
+    """Test a successful YAML import."""
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_IMPORT}, data={CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY
+    assert result["title"] == DEFAULT_HOST
+    assert result["data"] == {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("connected", "connect_error"), CONNECT_ERRORS)
+async def test_import_cannot_connect(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    connected: bool,
+    connect_error: ClientError | None,
+) -> None:
+    """Test failed YAML imports do not create entries."""
+    mock_router.success_init = connected
+    mock_router.async_connect.side_effect = connect_error
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_IMPORT}, data={CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.ABORT
+    assert result["reason"] == "cannot_connect"
+    assert not hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("source", [SOURCE_USER, SOURCE_IMPORT])
+async def test_already_configured(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    source: str,
+) -> None:
+    """Test config aborts when the host is already configured."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": source}, data={CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.ABORT
+    assert result["reason"] == "already_configured"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_setup_entry", "mock_router")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("source", [SOURCE_USER, SOURCE_IMPORT])
+async def test_different_host(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    source: str,
+) -> None:
+    """Test config allows adding a different host."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": source}, data={CONF_HOST: "192.168.0.1"}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY
+    assert result["title"] == "192.168.0.1"
+    assert result["data"] == {CONF_HOST: "192.168.0.1"}
+    assert len(hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)) == 2

+"""Tests for Sky Hub device trackers."""
+
+from datetime import timedelta
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock
+
+from freezegun.api import FrozenDateTimeFactory
+import pytest
+from pytest_homeassistant.common import MockConfigEntry, async_fire_time_changed
+
+from homeassistant.components.sky_hub.const import DEFAULT_HOST, DOMAIN
+from homeassistant.components.sky_hub.device_tracker import async_setup_scanner
+from homeassistant.config_entries import SOURCE_IMPORT
+from homeassistant.const import CONF_HOST, STATE_HOME, STATE_NOT_HOME, STATE_UNAVAILABLE
+from homeassistant.core import DOMAIN as HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN, HomeAssistant
+from homeassistant.helpers import entity_registry as er, issue_registry as ir
+from homeassistant.setup import async_setup_component
+
+from .conftest import LAPTOP, PHONE, MockDevice
+
+
+def _yaml_import_issue_id(host: str) -> str:
+    """Return the YAML import issue ID for a host."""
+    return f"yaml_import_cannot_connect_{host}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_router")
+async def test_legacy_setup(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    issue_registry: ir.IssueRegistry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test YAML setup imports a config entry and reports deprecation."""
+    await async_setup_component(
+        hass,
+        "device_tracker",
+        {"device_tracker": {"platform": DOMAIN, CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}},
+    )
+
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    entries = hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
+    assert len(entries) == 1
+    assert entries[0].source == SOURCE_IMPORT
+    assert entries[0].data == {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}
+
+    issue = issue_registry.async_get_issue(
+        HOMEASSISTANT_DOMAIN, f"deprecated_yaml_{DOMAIN}"
+    )
+    assert issue is not None
+    assert issue.severity is ir.IssueSeverity.WARNING
+    assert issue.translation_key == "deprecated_yaml"
+
+
+async def test_legacy_setup_cannot_connect(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    issue_registry: ir.IssueRegistry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test failed YAML imports report an issue."""
+    mock_router.success_init = False
+
+    await async_setup_component(
+        hass,
+        "device_tracker",
+        {"device_tracker": {"platform": DOMAIN, CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}},
+    )
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    assert not hass.config_entries.async_entries(DOMAIN)
+
+    issue = issue_registry.async_get_issue(DOMAIN, _yaml_import_issue_id(DEFAULT_HOST))
+    assert issue is not None
+    assert issue.severity is ir.IssueSeverity.ERROR
+    assert issue.translation_key == "yaml_import_cannot_connect"
+    assert issue.translation_placeholders == {"host": DEFAULT_HOST}
+
+
+async def test_legacy_setup_clears_connection_issue(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    issue_registry: ir.IssueRegistry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test a successful YAML import clears an earlier connection issue."""
+    mock_router.success_init = False
+    await async_setup_scanner(hass, {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}, AsyncMock())
+    assert (
+        issue_registry.async_get_issue(DOMAIN, _yaml_import_issue_id(DEFAULT_HOST))
+        is not None
+    )
+
+    mock_router.success_init = True
+    await async_setup_scanner(hass, {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}, AsyncMock())
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+    assert (
+        issue_registry.async_get_issue(DOMAIN, _yaml_import_issue_id(DEFAULT_HOST))
+        is None
+    )
+
+
+async def test_legacy_setup_connection_issues_are_host_specific(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    issue_registry: ir.IssueRegistry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test connection issues are tracked independently per YAML host."""
+    other_host = "192.168.0.1"
+
+    mock_router.success_init = False
+    await async_setup_scanner(hass, {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}, AsyncMock())
+    await async_setup_scanner(hass, {CONF_HOST: other_host}, AsyncMock())
+
+    issue_default = issue_registry.async_get_issue(
+        DOMAIN, _yaml_import_issue_id(DEFAULT_HOST)
+    )
+    issue_other = issue_registry.async_get_issue(
+        DOMAIN, _yaml_import_issue_id(other_host)
+    )
+
+    assert issue_default is not None
+    assert issue_default.translation_placeholders == {"host": DEFAULT_HOST}
+    assert issue_other is not None
+    assert issue_other.translation_placeholders == {"host": other_host}
+
+
+async def test_legacy_setup_success_only_clears_matching_host_issue(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    issue_registry: ir.IssueRegistry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test success for one host does not clear another host's issue."""
+    other_host = "192.168.0.1"
+
+    mock_router.success_init = False
+    await async_setup_scanner(hass, {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}, AsyncMock())
+    await async_setup_scanner(hass, {CONF_HOST: other_host}, AsyncMock())
+
+    mock_router.success_init = True
+    await async_setup_scanner(hass, {CONF_HOST: DEFAULT_HOST}, AsyncMock())
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    assert (
+        issue_registry.async_get_issue(DOMAIN, _yaml_import_issue_id(DEFAULT_HOST))
+        is None
+    )
+    assert (
+        issue_registry.async_get_issue(DOMAIN, _yaml_import_issue_id(other_host))
+        is not None
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("entity_registry_enabled_by_default", "mock_router")
+async def test_setup_entry(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    entity_registry: er.EntityRegistry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test initial devices create tracker entities with names and identifiers."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    state = hass.states.get("device_tracker.laptop")
+    assert state is not None
+    assert state.state == STATE_HOME
+    assert state.attributes["host_name"] == LAPTOP.name
+    assert state.attributes["mac"] == LAPTOP.mac
+
+    registry_entry = entity_registry.async_get("device_tracker.laptop")
+    assert registry_entry is not None
+    assert registry_entry.unique_id == f"{mock_config_entry.entry_id}_{LAPTOP.mac}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("entity_registry_enabled_by_default")
+async def test_new_device_discovered(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    freezer: FrozenDateTimeFactory,
+) -> None:
+    """Test devices discovered during polling create new tracker entities."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    assert hass.states.get("device_tracker.laptop").state == STATE_HOME
+    assert hass.states.get("device_tracker.phone") is None
+    assert len(hass.states.async_all("device_tracker")) == 1
+
+    mock_router.async_get_skyhub_data.return_value = [LAPTOP, PHONE]
+    freezer.tick(timedelta(seconds=31))
+    async_fire_time_changed(hass)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)
+
+    assert hass.states.get("device_tracker.laptop").state == STATE_HOME
+    assert hass.states.get("device_tracker.phone").state == STATE_HOME
+    assert len(hass.states.async_all("device_tracker")) == 2
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("entity_registry_enabled_by_default")
+async def test_device_disconnected(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    freezer: FrozenDateTimeFactory,
+) -> None:
+    """Test devices missing from a successful scan become not home."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    assert hass.states.get("device_tracker.laptop").state == STATE_HOME
+
+    mock_router.async_get_skyhub_data.return_value = [PHONE]
+    freezer.tick(timedelta(seconds=31))
+    async_fire_time_changed(hass)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)
+
+    assert hass.states.get("device_tracker.laptop").state == STATE_NOT_HOME
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("entity_registry_enabled_by_default")
+async def test_scan_failure(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    freezer: FrozenDateTimeFactory,
+) -> None:
+    """Test a failed scan makes existing tracker entities unavailable."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    mock_router.async_get_skyhub_data.return_value = None
+    freezer.tick(timedelta(seconds=31))
+    async_fire_time_changed(hass)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)
+
+    assert hass.states.get("device_tracker.laptop").state == STATE_UNAVAILABLE
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("entity_registry_enabled_by_default")
+async def test_device_name_updated(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    freezer: FrozenDateTimeFactory,
+) -> None:
+    """Test a device name change updates the existing tracker entity."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    mock_router.async_get_skyhub_data.return_value = [
+        MockDevice(LAPTOP.mac, "Work laptop")
+    ]
+    freezer.tick(timedelta(seconds=31))
+    async_fire_time_changed(hass)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done(wait_background_tasks=True)
+
+    assert hass.states.get("device_tracker.laptop").state == STATE_HOME
+    assert (
+        hass.states.get("device_tracker.laptop").attributes["host_name"]
+        == "Work laptop"
+    )
+    assert len(hass.states.async_all("device_tracker")) == 1

+"""Tests for the Sky Hub integration."""
+
+from datetime import timedelta
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+from freezegun.api import FrozenDateTimeFactory
+import pytest
+from pytest_homeassistant.common import MockConfigEntry, async_fire_time_changed
+
+from homeassistant.components.device_tracker.legacy import YAML_DEVICES, Device
+from homeassistant.components.sky_hub.const import (
+    DEFAULT_HOST,
+    DOMAIN,
+    ISSUE_LEGACY_KNOWN_DEVICES,
+)
+from homeassistant.components.sky_hub.coordinator import SCAN_INTERVAL
+from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntryState
+from homeassistant.const import CONF_HOST
+from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
+from homeassistant.helpers import issue_registry as ir
+
+from .conftest import LAPTOP, PHONE
+
+
+def _issue_id(entry_id: str) -> str:
+    """Return the per-entry issue ID for the legacy known_devices repair."""
+    return f"{ISSUE_LEGACY_KNOWN_DEVICES}_{entry_id}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_router")
+async def test_unload_entry(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test unloading a config entry."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    assert await hass.config_entries.async_unload(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+
+async def test_setup_entry_cannot_connect(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+) -> None:
+    """Test setup retries when the router cannot connect."""
+    mock_router.success_init = False
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+    await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    assert mock_config_entry.state is ConfigEntryState.SETUP_RETRY
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_router")
+async def test_legacy_known_devices_issue(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    issue_registry: ir.IssueRegistry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test tracked legacy devices raise a conflict issue."""
+    legacy_devices = [
+        Device(hass, timedelta(0), True, "laptop", LAPTOP.mac),
+    ]
+
+    with patch(
+        "homeassistant.components.sky_hub.async_load_config",
+        return_value=legacy_devices,
+    ):
+        mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+        await hass.config_entries.async_setup(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+        await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    issue = issue_registry.async_get_issue(
+        DOMAIN, _issue_id(mock_config_entry.entry_id)
+    )
+    assert issue is not None
+    assert issue.severity is ir.IssueSeverity.ERROR
+    assert issue.is_fixable is False
+    assert issue.translation_key == ISSUE_LEGACY_KNOWN_DEVICES
+    assert issue.translation_placeholders == {
+        "host": DEFAULT_HOST,
+        "path": YAML_DEVICES,
+        "devices": "- `laptop`",
+    }
+
+
+@pytest.mark.usefixtures("mock_router")
+async def test_legacy_known_devices_no_issue(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    issue_registry: ir.IssueRegistry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test untracked and unrelated known_devices.yaml entries are ignored."""
+    legacy_devices = [
+        Device(hass, timedelta(0), False, "laptop", LAPTOP.mac),
+        Device(hass, timedelta(0), True, "other_router_device", PHONE.mac),
+    ]
+
+    with patch(
+        "homeassistant.components.sky_hub.async_load_config",
+        return_value=legacy_devices,

+        mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)

+        await hass.async_block_till_done()
+
+    assert (
+        issue_registry.async_get_issue(DOMAIN, _issue_id(mock_config_entry.entry_id))
+        is None
+    )
+
+
+async def test_legacy_known_devices_issue_on_new_device(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+    mock_router: MagicMock,
+    issue_registry: ir.IssueRegistry,
+    freezer: FrozenDateTimeFactory,
+) -> None:
+    """Test a device discovered after setup raises a legacy conflict issue."""
+    legacy_devices = [Device(hass, timedelta(0), True, "phone", PHONE.mac)]
+
+    with patch(
+        "homeassistant.components.sky_hub.async_load_config",
+        return_value=legacy_devices,
+    ):

+    SelectSelectorMode,

+

+
+STEP_USER_DATA_SCHEMA = probatio.Schema(
+    {
+        probatio.Required(CONF_HOST): str,
+        probatio.Required(CONF_USERNAME): str,
+        probatio.Required(probatio.Secret(CONF_PASSWORD)): str,
+        probatio.Required(
+            CONF_DHCP_SOFTWARE, default=DEFAULT_DHCP_SOFTWARE
+        ): SelectSelector(
+            SelectSelectorConfig(
+                options=DHCP_SOFTWARES,
+                translation_key="dhcp_software",
+                mode=SelectSelectorMode.DROPDOWN,
+            )
+        ),
+    }
+)
+

+def validate_connection(data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Validate that we can log in to the router with the given configuration."""
+    ubus = Ubus(
+        f"http://{data[CONF_HOST]}/ubus",
+        data[CONF_USERNAME],
+        data[CONF_PASSWORD],
+    )
+    try:
+        session_id = ubus.connect()
+    except PermissionError as err:
+        raise InvalidAuth from err
+    except (ConnectionError, TypeError) as err:
+        # openwrt-ubus-rpc raises TypeError when the HTTP request itself fails.
+        raise CannotConnect from err
+    if session_id is None:
+        raise InvalidAuth
+

+    """Handle a config flow for OpenWrt (ubus)."""
+
+    VERSION = 1
+
+    @override

+        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
+    ) -> ConfigFlowResult:
+        """Handle the initial step."""
+        errors: dict[str, str] = {}
+        if user_input is not None:
+            self._async_abort_entries_match({CONF_HOST: user_input[CONF_HOST]})
+            try:
+                await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(validate_connection, user_input)
+            except CannotConnect:
+                errors["base"] = "cannot_connect"
+            except InvalidAuth:
+                errors["base"] = "invalid_auth"

+

+"""DataUpdateCoordinator for the OpenWrt (ubus) integration."""
+
+from datetime import timedelta
+import logging
+from typing import override
+
+from openwrt.ubus import Ubus
+
+from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntry
+from homeassistant.const import CONF_HOST, CONF_PASSWORD, CONF_USERNAME

+
+from .const import CONF_DHCP_SOFTWARE, DOMAIN

+_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+UPDATE_INTERVAL = timedelta(seconds=30)
+
+type UbusConfigEntry = ConfigEntry[UbusDataUpdateCoordinator]
+
+
+class UbusDataUpdateCoordinator(DataUpdateCoordinator[dict[str, str | None]]):
+    """Fetch the authorized wireless clients from an OpenWrt router over ubus."""
+
+    config_entry: UbusConfigEntry
+
+    def __init__(self, hass: HomeAssistant, config_entry: UbusConfigEntry) -> None:
+        """Initialize the coordinator from a config entry."""
+        self.host: str = config_entry.data[CONF_HOST]
+        self.dhcp_software: str = config_entry.data[CONF_DHCP_SOFTWARE]
+        self.ubus = Ubus(
+            f"http://{self.host}/ubus",
+            config_entry.data[CONF_USERNAME],
+            config_entry.data[CONF_PASSWORD],
+        )
+        self._hostapd: list[str] = []
+        self._leasefile: str | None = None
+        self._mac2name: dict[str, str] | None = None
+
+        super().__init__(
+            hass,
+            _LOGGER,
+            config_entry=config_entry,
+            name=f"{DOMAIN} - {self.host}",
+            update_interval=UPDATE_INTERVAL,
+        )
+
+    @override
+    async def _async_update_data(self) -> dict[str, str | None]:
+        """Return the currently connected devices keyed by MAC address."""
+        return await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(self._update)
+
+    def _update(self) -> dict[str, str | None]:
+        """Query the router, re-authenticating once if the session expired."""
+        if self.ubus.session_id is None:
+            self._login()
+        try:
+            return self._read_clients()
+        except PermissionError:
+            # The router dropped our session (e.g. after a reboot); log back in.
+            self._login()
+        try:
+            return self._read_clients()
+        except PermissionError as err:
+            raise UpdateFailed(f"Access denied by ubus at {self.host}") from err
+
+    def _login(self) -> None:
+        """Open a ubus session, raising UpdateFailed on failure."""
+        try:
+            session_id = self.ubus.connect()
+        except (ConnectionError, PermissionError, TypeError) as err:
+            # openwrt-ubus-rpc raises TypeError when the HTTP request itself
+            # fails, because it subscripts a None response.
+            raise UpdateFailed(f"Error connecting to ubus at {self.host}") from err
+        if session_id is None:
+            raise UpdateFailed(f"Invalid credentials for ubus at {self.host}")
+
+    def _read_clients(self) -> dict[str, str | None]:
+        """Return authorized clients mapped to their DHCP hostname.
+
+        PermissionError is left to propagate so the caller can re-authenticate.
+        """
+        clients = self._fetch_hostapd_clients()
+        if self._mac2name is None:
+            self._mac2name = self._generate_mac2name()
+        return {
+            mac: self._name_for(mac)
+            for mac, client in clients.items()
+            if client["authorized"]
+        }
+
+    def _fetch_hostapd_clients(self) -> dict[str, dict]:
+        """Return the raw hostapd client table merged across all interfaces."""
+        try:
+            if not self._hostapd:
+                if not (hostapd := self.ubus.get_hostapd()):
+                    raise UpdateFailed(f"No hostapd data from ubus at {self.host}")
+                self._hostapd = list(hostapd)
+            clients: dict[str, dict] = {}
+            for interface in self._hostapd:
+                if result := self.ubus.get_hostapd_clients(interface):
+                    clients.update(result["clients"])
+        except ConnectionError as err:
+            raise UpdateFailed(f"Error querying ubus at {self.host}") from err
+        return clients
+
+    def _name_for(self, mac: str) -> str | None:
+        """Return the DHCP hostname for a MAC address, if known."""
+        if self._mac2name is None:
+            return None
+        return self._mac2name.get(mac.upper())
+
+    def _generate_mac2name(self) -> dict[str, str] | None:
+        """Build the MAC-to-hostname map for the configured DHCP software."""
+        if self.dhcp_software == "dnsmasq":
+            return self._dnsmasq_mac2name()
+        if self.dhcp_software == "odhcpd":
+            return self._odhcpd_mac2name()
+        return {}
+
+    def _dnsmasq_mac2name(self) -> dict[str, str] | None:
+        """Read the dnsmasq lease file. Returns None to retry if unavailable."""
+        try:
+            if self._leasefile is None:
+                if not (result := self.ubus.get_uci_config("dhcp", "dnsmasq")):
+                    return None
+                self._leasefile = next(iter(result["values"].values()))["leasefile"]
+            result = self.ubus.file_read(self._leasefile)
+        except ConnectionError as err:
+            raise UpdateFailed(
+                f"Error reading leases from ubus at {self.host}"
+            ) from err
+
+        if not result:
+            return None
+
+        mac2name = {}
+        for line in result["data"].splitlines():
+            hosts = line.split(" ")
+            mac2name[hosts[1].upper()] = hosts[3]
+        return mac2name
+
+    def _odhcpd_mac2name(self) -> dict[str, str] | None:
+        """Read the odhcpd leases. Returns None to retry if unavailable."""
+        try:
+            result = self.ubus.get_dhcp_method("ipv4leases")
+        except ConnectionError as err:
+            raise UpdateFailed(
+                f"Error reading leases from ubus at {self.host}"
+            ) from err
+
+        if not result:
+            return None
+
+        mac2name = {}
+        for device in result["device"].values():
+            for lease in device["leases"]:
+                mac = ":".join(
+                    lease["mac"][i : i + 2] for i in range(0, len(lease["mac"]), 2)
+                )
+                mac2name[mac.upper()] = lease["hostname"]
+        return mac2name

+"""Tests for the OpenWrt (ubus) config flow."""
+
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock
+
+import pytest
+from pytest_homeassistant.common import MockConfigEntry
+
+from homeassistant.components.ubus.const import CONF_DHCP_SOFTWARE, DOMAIN
+from homeassistant.config_entries import SOURCE_IMPORT, SOURCE_USER
+from homeassistant.const import CONF_HOST, CONF_PASSWORD, CONF_USERNAME
+from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
+from homeassistant.data_entry_flow import FlowResultType
+
+from .conftest import MOCK_CONFIG, MOCK_HOST
+
+USER_INPUT = {
+    CONF_HOST: MOCK_HOST,
+    CONF_USERNAME: "root",
+    CONF_PASSWORD: "password",
+}
+
+
+async def test_user_flow_success(
+    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_setup_entry: AsyncMock, mock_ubus: MagicMock
+) -> None:
+    """Test the user flow creates an entry with the default DHCP software."""
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_USER}
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.FORM
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
+        result["flow_id"], user_input=USER_INPUT
+    )
+
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY
+    assert result["title"] == MOCK_HOST
+    assert result["data"] == MOCK_CONFIG
+
+
+async def test_user_flow_cannot_connect(
+    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_setup_entry: AsyncMock, mock_ubus: MagicMock
+) -> None:
+    """Test the user flow recovers after a connection error."""
+    mock_ubus.return_value.connect.side_effect = ConnectionError("boom")
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_USER}
+    )
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
+        result["flow_id"], user_input=USER_INPUT
+    )
+
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.FORM
+    assert result["errors"] == {"base": "cannot_connect"}
+
+    mock_ubus.return_value.connect.side_effect = None
+    mock_ubus.return_value.connect.return_value = "session-id"
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
+        result["flow_id"], user_input=USER_INPUT
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "connect",
+    [
+        pytest.param(
+            {"side_effect": PermissionError("Access denied")}, id="access_denied"
+        ),
+        pytest.param({"side_effect": None, "return_value": None}, id="no_session"),
+    ],
+)
+async def test_user_flow_invalid_auth(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_setup_entry: AsyncMock,
+    mock_ubus: MagicMock,
+    connect: dict,
+) -> None:
+    """Test the user flow reports invalid credentials and then recovers."""
+    mock_ubus.return_value.connect.configure_mock(**connect)
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_USER}
+    )
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
+        result["flow_id"], user_input=USER_INPUT
+    )
+
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.FORM
+    assert result["errors"] == {"base": "invalid_auth"}
+
+    mock_ubus.return_value.connect.configure_mock(
+        side_effect=None, return_value="session-id"
+    )
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
+        result["flow_id"], user_input=USER_INPUT
+    )
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY
+
+
+async def test_user_flow_already_configured(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_setup_entry: AsyncMock,
+    mock_ubus: MagicMock,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test the user flow aborts when the host is already configured."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_USER}
+    )
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
+        result["flow_id"], user_input=USER_INPUT
+    )
+
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.ABORT
+    assert result["reason"] == "already_configured"
+
+
+async def test_import_flow(
+    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_setup_entry: AsyncMock, mock_ubus: MagicMock
+) -> None:
+    """Test importing a YAML configuration."""
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_IMPORT}, data=MOCK_CONFIG
+    )
+
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY
+    assert result["title"] == MOCK_HOST
+    assert result["data"] == MOCK_CONFIG
+
+
+async def test_import_flow_already_configured(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_setup_entry: AsyncMock,
+    mock_ubus: MagicMock,
+    mock_config_entry: MockConfigEntry,
+) -> None:
+    """Test the import flow aborts when the host is already configured."""
+    mock_config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
+
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_IMPORT}, data=MOCK_CONFIG
+    )
+
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.ABORT
+    assert result["reason"] == "already_configured"
+
+
+async def test_import_flow_preserves_dhcp_software(
+    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_setup_entry: AsyncMock, mock_ubus: MagicMock
+) -> None:
+    """Test a non-default DHCP software choice survives the import."""
+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN,
+        context={"source": SOURCE_IMPORT},
+        data={**MOCK_CONFIG, CONF_DHCP_SOFTWARE: "odhcpd"},
+    )
+
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.CREATE_ENTRY
+    assert result["data"][CONF_DHCP_SOFTWARE] == "odhcpd"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("side_effect", "reason"),
+    [
+        pytest.param(TypeError, "cannot_connect", id="cannot_connect"),
+        pytest.param(PermissionError, "invalid_auth", id="invalid_auth"),
+    ],
+)
+async def test_import_flow_errors(
+    hass: HomeAssistant,
+    mock_setup_entry: AsyncMock,
+    mock_ubus: MagicMock,
+    side_effect: type[Exception],
+    reason: str,
+) -> None:
+    """Test the import flow aborts when the router can't be logged in to."""
+    mock_ubus.return_value.connect.side_effect = side_effect

+    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_init(
+        DOMAIN, context={"source": SOURCE_IMPORT}, data=MOCK_CONFIG
+    )
+
+    assert result["type"] is FlowResultType.ABORT
+    assert result["reason"] == reason
